criterion_text: Peer-reviewed journal or conference paper; accepted 2025--2026 main-conference, findings, and workshop papers were eligible but their publication category was recorded separately.
Proposes, evaluates, or critically benchmarks a computational method for scene anomaly detection, visual hazard recognition, or camera/video-feed integrity.

Targets surveillance, traffic monitoring, public-space monitoring, industrial monitoring, or a fixed-camera setting whose sensing conditions, anomaly definition, and evaluation outputs transfer directly to surveillance feed monitoring.
Reports quantitative evaluation on a public benchmark or a sufficiently described study-specific evaluation corpus.
Falls within January 2010--June 2026, except seminal pre-2010 datasets or methods required for technical context.
Non-English publication or inaccessible full text.
Duplicate report, extended abstract, or a conference version superseded by a substantially overlapping journal extension.
Non-visual-only work, medical/industrial inspection without a surveillance transfer argument, or generic anomaly detection without relevant evaluation.
No quantitative evaluation, inadequate description of data/splits, or results that cannot be associated with a defined task and metric.
Review papers used only for positioning, not as primary experimental evidence.
